josh_customer: Exported billing CSV from Console -> Analytics -> Exports for last 30 days. File downloaded but Excel shows a blank sheet and filesize is 1.2KB. Opening in VSCode shows lots of NUL bytes between characters. Anyone seen this?

sara_support: Sorry about that — can you paste the exact filename and the download link (or attach a small sample)? Which browser/OS?

josh_customer: Filename: billing-usage-20260310.csv size: 1,248 bytes. Windows 10, Excel 2016 (Office 365), Chrome 114. I can't attach here, but hex preview from a quick dump: 
00 62 00 69 00 6c 00 6c 00 69 00 6e 00 67 00 2c 00 75 00 73 00 61 00 67 00 65 00 2c 00 74 00 6f 00 6b 00 65 00 6e 00

mike_engineer: That hex (00 between bytes) == UTF-16LE encoding. We recently shipped a change so the CSV export generator writes UTF-16LE for "CSV (Excel)" to improve Excel compatibility. Looks like the writer didn't emit the BOM for some code paths. Excel often treats no-BOM UTF-16 as an unknown encoding and shows an empty sheet. Can you try Data -> Get Data -> From Text/CSV and choose "65001: Unicode (UTF-8)" or better "1200: UTF-16 LE"? Quick workaround: open in Notepad and Save As -> choose UTF-8 then reopen in Excel.

sara_support: Repro steps for us: Console -> Analytics -> Exports -> choose CSV (Excel) -> Export -> click download. We see export_service v2.14.3 reported format=UTF-16LE. Are you seeing only header row or also data rows?

josh_customer: I expected ~11 rows, but when I open in Excel it looks empty. In a hex viewer I can see the header and a few rows, so data is there, just not decoded by Excel.

export_service_bot: export job 98765 finished: status=success, rows=11, format=UTF-16LE, written_bytes=1248, s3_key=exports/2026/03/10/billing-usage-98765.csv

mike_engineer: OK the service metadata confirms UTF-16LE. Root cause: writer emits UTF-16LE but omits the BOM for small-buffer path (rows < 100) due to a bug in the stream wrapper. Fix plan: always write BOM for UTF-16LE and add unit/integration tests to catch no-BOM output. Workaround for customers: Import via Excel's Text Import Wizard and pick "Unicode (UTF-16 LE)" or open in Notepad++ -> Encoding -> Convert to UTF-8.

hana_product: FYI we'll need a short KB article describing the workaround and an item in Release Notes for the hotfix. Also consider switching default to UTF-8 with BOM for CSV exports to avoid Excel quirks.

sara_support: I'll reply to the customer with the import steps and offer to regenerate the export after we deploy the fix. @mike_engineer can you estimate ETA for hotfix?

mike_engineer: Creating ticket INFR-4532 and PR #2897. I can get a hotfix ready for staging in ~2 business days, then canary to prod same day if tests pass. Will post updates here. :memo:

josh_customer: Thanks — importing as UTF-16LE worked. If you can regenerate the file that'd be great, otherwise I'm fine using the import steps. :white_check_mark:

sara_support: Great — closing the loop once hotfix is deployed and regenerated export uploaded. Thanks everyone! :thumbsup:
